oneLiner: The End has no breathable air: your air bubbles drain while you are there and you start taking damage once they run out, unless you carry a Create backtank (by default a diving helmet is required alongside it) or stand in Conduit Power, e.g. from an End Conduit.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Create backtanks (read via BacktankUtil.getAllWithAir/getAir/consumeAir) are the only gear that supplies air in the End, and the client draws a backtank item + MM:SS remaining-time overlay next to the hotbar. Without Create, CreateCompat.isLoaded() is false, the backtank branch is skipped entirely and the module degrades to plain breath-holding (plus Conduit Power and Water Breathing). No shouldInitialize() gate, so the module itself always loads. README states the same: 'Fully functional - Create backtanks just can't supply air in the End'.

shortDescription: Removes oxygen from the End dimension, requiring players to hold their breath or use gear.
notes:
MECHANIC (EndOxygenModule.onLivingBreathe, only for Player, only Level.END, skipped in creative/spectator):
1) Conduit Power branch (if conduit_power_grants_air): setCanBreathe(true) + setRefillAirAmount(getMaxAirSupply()) and `return` - this branch also skips the damage block entirely. The effect source in this mod is the end_conduit module (EndConduitBlockEntity.java:167 adds MobEffects.CONDUIT_POWER, 260 ticks, amplifier 0, ambient+visible) - a real, load-bearing cross-module coupling.
2) Air is floored at 1 (`if (getAirSupply() < 1) setAirSupply(1)`), applied every tick before the event's own consumption, so the bar never walks down to vanilla's drowning threshold; all damage comes from this module.
3) Backtank branch (Create only): canBreathe=true, setRefillAirAmount(1), and every `backtank.backtank_depletion_rate` ticks 1 air is consumed from the FIRST backtank in the list (backtanks.get(0)). depletionRate == 0 disables consumption entirely -> an infinite tank.
4) Otherwise canBreathe=false and 1 air is consumed only when `player.tickCount % (air_consumption_interval + (WaterBreathing amplifier + 1) * water_breathing_effect_interval_bonus) == 0`, else setConsumeAirAmount(0). Note this is keyed off the player entity's free-running `tickCount`, NOT a countdown that restarts when you enter the End - the phase is whatever the entity's age happens to be. With defaults (interval 2, vanilla max air 300) that is ~600 ticks / ~30 s of grace before damage starts.
5) Damage: when `getAirSupply() <= 1 && tickCount % damage_tick == 0`, hurt with DamageSource vanillaplusadditions:out_of_oxygen (data/vanillaplusadditions/damage_type/out_of_oxygen.json: exhaustion 0.1, message_id vanillaplusadditions.out_of_oxygen, scaling when_caused_by_living_non_player; death message lang key `death.attack.vanillaplusadditions.out_of_oxygen` = "%1$s ran out of oxygen", en_us.json:84). `EndOxygenConfig.getOutOfAirDamage()` narrows the DoubleValue to a float for `player.hurt`.

LIKELY BUG / DOC CONTRADICTION - the diving-helmet tag has no data file. `EndOxygenModule.DIVING_HELMETS` = TagKey `vanillaplusadditions:diving_helmets` (EndOxygenModule.java:40-43), and with the DEFAULT `backtank.requires_full_set = true` the backtank only works when the HEAD-slot item is in that tag (EndOxygenModule.java:88-90). The repo ships no such tag JSON: the only file under src/main/resources/data/vanillaplusadditions/tags/item/ is arm_goggles.json, a repo-wide find for tag JSONs (including world_datapacks/) turns up nothing named diving_helmets or backtanks, and grepping the whole repo finds "diving_helmets" only in EndOxygenModule.java and docs/modules/end_oxygen.md. There is no datagen in the project (no GatherDataEvent / TagsProvider / DataGenerator anywhere). So unless an external datapack on the server populates the tag, backtanks never grant air with default config; setting requires_full_set=false is the only in-repo-provable way to make them work. Verified independently in this pass - worth confirming in game before documenting the helmet requirement as functional.

DEAD CODE: `EndOxygenModule.BACKTANKS` (TagKey `vanillaplusadditions:backtanks`, EndOxygenModule.java:35-38) is declared public static final and never read by any class in the repo. Backtank detection runs purely through Create's BacktankUtil. docs/modules/end_oxygen.md:38-39 ("`vanillaplusadditions:backtanks` and `vanillaplusadditions:diving_helmets` item tags control which items count") is therefore wrong for backtanks and unbacked for helmets.

DOCS OUT OF DATE: docs/modules/end_oxygen.md's config table lists 6 keys and is missing `conduit_power_grants_air` (added 2026-07-22 in d73a4b0 together with end_conduit, first released in v1.0.0-beta.46). Its "Requirements" section calls Create a requirement - it is optional (mods.toml:80-87, type="optional"). README.md:304 still links docs/end_oxygen.md while the file now lives at docs/modules/end_oxygen.md (doc restructure currently uncommitted in the working tree).

CLIENT HUD HACK: EndOxygenClientEvents.onRenderGuiLayer (Pre, layer minecraft:air_level) mutates the local player's air (`setAirSupply(max - 1)` when air is full) purely so vanilla's air-bubble layer renders at all in the End - a client-side display trick, resynced by the server. The Post hook draws the first air-holding backtank's item at guiWidth/2+90, guiHeight-53 (+9 when the stack has DataComponents.FIRE_RESISTANT, i.e. netherite backtank) with an MM:SS timer computed from `max(0, air - 1) * backtank_depletion_rate / level.tickRateManager().tickrate()`, capped at 99:59; when backtank_depletion_rate == 0 it hardcodes totalSeconds = 5999 (displays 99:59); the text flashes red when `air < 60 && air % 2 == 0`. The whole overlay returns early unless CreateCompat.isLoaded(). This class is registered by annotation (@EventBusSubscriber(value = Dist.CLIENT, bus = GAME)), independent of module initialization, and guards itself by looking the module up in ModuleManager at runtime (null + isModuleEnabled check).

DAMAGE QUIRKS worth a sentence in the docs: (a) the damage block is NOT inside an else - it also runs while breathing from a backtank, and since the backtank only refills 1 air per tick, a player who enters the End at air <= 1 keeps taking damage for a moment while the bar recovers; (b) out_of_oxygen is in no minecraft:bypasses_armor / bypasses_invulnerability tag - the repo ships no damage_type tag files at all - so unlike vanilla drowning this damage is reduced by armor and respects invulnerability frames.

CONFIG SAFETY: `EndOxygenConfig.conduitPowerGrantsAir()` returns `conduitPowerGrantsAir == null || conduitPowerGrantsAir.get()` - defaults to true if the spec value is not built yet; the other six getters have no such guard and would NPE in the same situation.

SIDES: the breathing handler is an instance handler on the common bus (`NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this)` in onInitialize), i.e. it runs on both physical sides; only the HUD class is Dist.CLIENT-only. So this module is genuinely "both", not client-only.

STANDALONE JAR: build.gradle:423-424 lists end_oxygen with dataGlobs ['data/vanillaplusadditions/damage_type/out_of_oxygen.json'], no mixins, no moduleDeps; entrypoint src/main/java/.../standalone/end_oxygen/EndOxygenStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_end_oxygen") -> StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot). The jar task includes modules/end_oxygen/** wholesale, so the client HUD class ships with it. The generated per-module neoforge.mods.toml (renderModuleToml, build.gradle:507-530) only declares vpa_core/neoforge/minecraft + 'incompatible' against the bundle - it does NOT declare the optional `create` dependency the bundle's mods.toml has. Per CHANGELOG [1.0.0-beta.72] (CHANGELOG.md:339-346) the Create gate was split into the Create-free CreateCompat class exactly so vpa_end_oxygen provably boots without Create (same class-linking trap that broke overpacked_extensions).

ORPHAN LANG KEYS: `message.action_bar.low_oxygen_alert` ("§cLOW OXYGEN ALERT") and `message.action_bar.remaining_oxygen` ("Remaining Oxygen: %s %s") sit in en_us.json:150-151 but no Java code anywhere references "action_bar" - apparently leftovers from an earlier oxygen HUD; do not document them as features.
